blockNote: Enemy combat stat rows (Bank 01, 109552-109992 = $01:ABF0): 110 rows of 4 bytes < HP, ATK, DEF, gemDropType >. The row number is the stats index: byte 6 of an enemy-spawn record in scene_actors (index $01-$63 in 62 distinct values; 0 = an actor without combat stats). InitActorFromSceneData stores index x 4 + the table address in statsPtr ($7F0020,X) and loads byte 0 into currentHp ($7F0026,X). Boss and special actors set statsPtr themselves with an operand such as enemy_stats_table+154 (the offset is in hex: +154 / 4 = row $55). The old note was wrong about the fourth byte ('Type 0-3, affects damage calculations'), about DEF $7F ('immune to normal damage') and about HP $7F / $FF ('boss-tier').
=== FIELDS (read by combat_collision and StandardEnemyDefeatHandler) ===
| Byte | Field | Reader |
| +0 | HP: the start value of currentHp and the maximum (hitVictimMaxHp) | InitActorFromSceneData, ApplyHitDamageToVictim |
| +1 | ATK: the damage the enemy deals to the player on contact: max(1, ATK - playerDef), then 60 frames of invulnerability | the enemy-hits-player path of combat_collision |
| +2 | DEF: subtracted from the player's total strength: rawDamage = max(1, totalStr - DEF), netDamage = rawDamage + characterForm | ApplyHitDamageToVictim (_DamagePath) |
| +3 | gemDropType: 0 = no gem, 1 = SpawnDropGem1, 2 = SpawnDropGem2, 3 or more = SpawnDropByHpTier (EnemyDropSystem) | EnemyGemDropRouter in StandardEnemyDefeatHandler |

PlayerAttackHitTest (the player's attack box) does not read DEF: its damage is chainDamage / 2 + 1, with chainDamage accumulating over consecutive hits of one attack (formulas in the combat_collision header). Which attack of the game goes through which of the two routines was not traced at runtime (OQ-I066-2). DEF $7F (21 rows) and $FF (row $46) therefore do not make an enemy immune: in ApplyHitDamageToVictim they only pin every hit to its minimum, 1 + characterForm. Damage and stagger immunity are bits $0010 / $0020 of the actor's $12 flags (EnemyInitBasic sets both), not table data.
The gem is only dropped when the scene's clear reward (flag $0300) was already taken or other enemies remain; the last enemy of a scene gives the stat reward of enemy_clear_reward_table instead.
=== WHOLE-TABLE FACTS ===

- 18 rows are all zero ($00 $12 $13 $15-$17 $23-$26 $65-$68 $6A-$6D). Row $00 is also the pointer EnemyInitBasic stores: an actor whose statsPtr equals the table address is counted as 'no stats' (no kill counter, no gem, no reward).
- 92 rows have stats: gemDropType 0 in 37, 1 in 21, 2 in 21, 3 in 13. 21 rows have DEF $7F, row $46 has DEF $FF, rows $21 and $22 have HP $FF.

- Rows named by code (statsPtr operands): $01 dc2F_adrift; $08 ec0E_spiney; $11 ec12_skull_chaser and sp5A_phantom_ribber; $31 and $69 mu67_vampires; $33 gw82_archer; $37 gw8A_sand_fanger; $46 twelve switch, blocker and trapped-slave actors (hit_switch, dm3F_switch, dm40_trapped_slave, ec0E_switch, ec11_aqueduct_blocker, ec11_button_voice, ec12_aqueduct_enemy, ir21_switch, pyD6_vader_barrier_lower / upper, sg52_blocker_enemy_a / b); $47 and $48 awB0_zombie; $4D pyD2_haunt; $55-$58 sE8_dark_gaia (and unused_mode7_boss for $55-$57); $5F and $60 sEA_solid_arm; $64 ec0E_lily and ir29_castoth.
- 16 rows with stats are neither used by a scene spawn record nor named by code: $06 $07 $09 $1F $20 $21 $22 $38 $39 $3B $40 $41 $4B $52 $53 $59 (OQ-I066-1).
The enemy a row belongs to is the actor named in the spawn record, so the table does not say which enemy it describes.

enemy_stats_table: 110 enemy-stats rows < HP, ATK, DEF, gemDropType >, row index = the stats index of a scene_actors enemy-spawn record (byte 6; 0 = none). Field uses, the all-zero rows, the rows named by code and the 16 rows with no reader are in the block note.

blockNote: Aura Barrier orbital spriteset (Bank 17, 1544192-1544618 = $17:9000): 3 animations ($00-$02), 12 frame records, 12 sprite groups, 30 sub-sprites. Only user: AuraProjectileChild in attack_ability_system (COP SetMetasprite ( @spriteset_aura )); AuraOrbitalSpawner makes 2 or 4 of those actors (4 when the upgrade flag $0B1E is set) and moves them around the player. The old note said '4 animation frames for the rotating barrier sprites': the table holds 3 animations of 4 frames. The struct format is described in the spriteset_freedan block note.
=== ANIMATIONS ===
| Index | Shape | Played by |
| $00 | 4 frames, hold 7 (8 ticks each), 2 sub-sprites of 8x8 per frame (small sparks) | AnimOnce first, and last when the orbital shrinks |
| $01 | 4 frames, hold 7, 3 sub-sprites per frame (a 16x16 and two 8x8 in the first, three 8x8 in the others) | AnimOnce second, and first when the orbital shrinks |
| $02 | 4 frames, hold 7, 2 sub-sprites of 16x16 (frames 0, 1 and 3) or 4 of 8x8 (frame 2) | the loop that runs until the spawner overwrites the actor's function pointer with AuraProjectileShrink |

AuraProjectileChild stages $00 and $01 once (the orbital grows) and then loops $02; AuraProjectileShrink plays $01 and $00 once and hides the actor ($10 bit $2000). All 12 groups keep the default attack box $F8 $F0 $01 $01.
=== ART AND PALETTE ===

Every tile word is in $0440-$046F: tile numbers $40-$6F with the palette bits (9-11) = 2, i.e. sprite palette 2 (CGRAM $A0-$AF). AuraVramDmaLoader uploads $0600 bytes (48 tiles) of misc_fx_1CC480 to VRAM $4400 with COP AdhocVramDma, and AuraBarrierMain copies 7 colours of fx_palette_198090 to CGRAM $A9 ($A9-$AF); AuraBarrierPaletteFX cycles them. That VRAM $4400 is tile $40 of the first sprite name table assumes the sprite name base is $4000 (OBSEL was not traced, OQ-I066-3).
Checks: 426 bytes = 6 (table) + 3 x 18 (lists of 4 records + the hidden $FFFF) + 12 x 13 (group headers) + 30 x 7 (sub-sprites).

spriteset_aura: 3 pointers to the frame lists, indexed by the animation number staged by AuraProjectileChild / AuraProjectileShrink: $00 and $01 grow-in, $02 the looping orbit. See the block note.
sprite_set_179006: Animation $00: 4 frames, hold 7, groups sprite_group_17903C ... 17908D (two 8x8 sub-sprites each, tile words $0460-$0466). The first stage of the grow-in and the last of the shrink.
sprite_set_179018: Animation $01: 4 frames, hold 7, groups sprite_group_1790A8 ... 17910E (three sub-sprites each, tile words $044C-$044F, $045E-$045F, $0467-$046F). The second stage of the grow-in and the first of the shrink.
sprite_set_17902A: Animation $02: 4 frames, hold 7, groups sprite_group_179130 ... 17918F (16x16 pairs in frames 0, 1 and 3, four 8x8 tiles in frame 2). The loop that runs while the orbit is active.
sprite_group_17903C: Example group: animation $00, frame 0. Header: extents X 4 / 4, Y 8 / 8, default attack box, body box $FC $08 $F8 $16, 2 sub-sprites (8x8, tile words $0460 and $0464, offsets (0,8) and (8,0)).

blockNote: Shadow player spriteset (Bank 14, 1343488-1355931 = $14:8000): every frame the player can show in form 2. 76 animations ($00-$4B), 261 frame records, 168 sprite groups, 1273 sub-sprites (at most 14 per group). Chosen by body_table rows $02 and $03 (spriteset bank $94, art shad_sprites_1BC000; row $03 is a copy, OQ-I061-1); SetActorBody copies the table pointer and bank into the actor ($7F0006, $7F0008). The animation numbering is shared with spriteset_will and spriteset_freedan, and the struct format (table, frame list, group header, sub-sprite) is described once, in the spriteset_freedan block note.

The old header ('walking, idle, attack and liquify animation frames', 'Shadow's unique morph poses') named poses the code does not use: 'liquify' appears nowhere outside the headers of this file and spriteset_shadow_fx, and the table has the same 76 indices as the Freedan table. Shadow's separate mode body is spriteset_shadow_mode (body_table row $08) and the effect sprites are in spriteset_shadow_fx.
=== WHAT DIFFERS FROM THE FREEDAN TABLE (same indices, other frame counts) ===

- Idle $00-$07 and $10-$17 are one frame with hold 9 (10 ticks). The player scripts stage $10-$13 for Shadow only; they use groups of their own (for example $00 shows sprite_group_148544, $10 shows sprite_group_14857B).
- Walk $08-$0F is 6 frames of hold 7 (Freedan 4 frames).

- Climb poses: the vine cycle $19-$1B, the ladder idles $2A-$2B and $2E-$2F and the detach poses $30-$31 and $34-$35 are one-frame lists (Freedan: 4 frames each); the ladder move $2C-$2D and the shimmy $32-$33 are 6 frames (holds 7, 3, 3, 7, 3, 3; Freedan 20 and 5); $18 is 4 frames (holds 9, 6, 4, 9). Other lists: $1C is 11 frames (holds 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 0), $1D-$25 are one frame each, $26-$29 are 4 frames.

- Melee attack $36-$39 is 7 frames (holds 3, 2, 1, 0, 0, 1, 2 = 16 ticks), the same frame count as Freedan; guard $3A-$3D is 8 frames of hold 0 (Freedan 4); $42-$43 and $48-$49 are 7 frames, $44-$47 and $4A-$4B one frame of hold 0.
- $3E-$41 (7 frames, holds 3, 1, 8, 4, 3, 3, 8) is not staged by the player scripts.
=== CHECKS ===

All 168 groups have a count byte equal to their number of sub-sprites, all 168 keep the default attack box $F8 $F0 $01 $01, all are referenced, all 76 frame lists are 4n + 2 bytes long (the label spacing of 75 consecutive lists was checked by hand) and 12443 bytes = 152 (table) + 4 x 261 + 2 x 76 (lists and their hidden $FFFF terminators) + 13 x 168 + 7 x 1273.

spriteset_shadow: 76 word pointers to frame lists, indexed by the actor animation index ($28); the same index space as spriteset_freedan (see its table part note for the staged indices). The Shadow shapes are listed in the block note: idle 1 frame (hold 9), walk 6 frames (hold 7), melee 7 frames, guard 8 frames of hold 0; the vine cycle and the ladder idles are single frames.
sprite_group_148544: Example group: Shadow idle south, the only frame of animation $00. Header: extents X 16 / 16, Y 45 / 8, default attack and body boxes, 6 sub-sprites of 16x16 (tile words $0000, $0020, $0102, $0100, $0022, $000E; $0102 and $0100 use the second name table, bit 8).
